title: Verifier-Guided Prompting for Intent-to-Configuration Translation: A Preregistered NetOps Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory trial to test whether constrained prompting plus a deterministic verifier-guided generate→verify→repair loop (one allowed repair) increases deterministic-verifier semantic-correctness when translating operator natural-language intents into low-level device configurations. Design: N=150 synthetic intents from a deterministic generator; execution semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one sampled initial candidate reused across conditions); model = gpt-5-mini; deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5; at most one repair call per intent. Results (artifact-grounded): baseline = 149/150 (99.333%); guarded = 150/150 (100.0%); paired absolute difference = 0.006667 (≈0.67 percentage points); exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00, 0.02] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Provider accounting: completed episodes = 300; model_calls_used = 151; shared_initial_generation = 150; repair-stage invocations = 1. Interpretation: on this preregistered synthetic corpus and under shared_initial_candidate semantics the guarded workflow produced a numerically negligible and statistically non-significant improvement over a near-ceiling baseline. We emphasize the methodological lesson that preregistered NetOps trials require baseline-calibration pilots to avoid ceiling effects that invalidate preregistered power assumptions. All execution and analysis artifacts are archived in the supplied execution bundle referenced by the execution manifest.

sections.introduction:
Natural-language intent interfaces aim to reduce operator burden by letting humans express desired network changes as free text that is automatically translated into executable device configurations. Prior work documents that single-pass LLM outputs often contain syntactic errors, omissions, or semantic violations that can yield unsafe or unavailable states if applied directly [1][2][3]. A widely discussed mitigation is a generate→verify→repair architecture in which an LLM produces a candidate, a deterministic verifier checks intent-level invariants, and an automated repair (or human gate) corrects violations before execution [4][5]. Security analyses additionally motivate deterministic gating because unchecked textual claims in multi-tool agents can become harmful actions [6].

Research question. After an autonomous literature review and preregistration we posed a confined confirmatory question: does constrained prompting (structured templates with explicit semantic slots) combined with deterministic verifier-guided iterative feedback materially increase verifier-level semantic correctness of NL→configuration translation versus an unconstrained baseline under a paired design? The trial (study_cand_2026_b2_v1) was preregistered and frozen prior to observing any model outputs.

Contributions. (1) A fully preregistered, artifactized paired confirmatory trial measuring deterministic-verifier pass/fail on a programmatically generated synthetic corpus (N=150 paired intents). (2) Artifact-backed outcomes showing that, under shared_initial_candidate semantics and a one-repair budget, the guarded pipeline raised verifier pass rate from 149/150 to 150/150 (+0.67 pp), a numerically negligible and statistically non-significant improvement (exact McNemar p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI = [0.00, 0.02]). (3) A methodological recommendation that preregistered NetOps trials include baseline-calibration pilots and explicitly specify generation semantics because semantics materially change the estimand and interpretation.
sections.related_work: Our literature synthesis focused on four lines relevant to verifier-guided NetOps pipelines. (i) Intent-to-configuration evaluations report that free-text prompts frequently produce omissions or incorrect sequencing that violate required invariants; published benchmarks and surveys document modest semantic-correctness rates and highlight prompt design and verifier choice as dominant factors [1][2]. (ii) Generate→verify→repair systems for IaC and configuration repair (e.g., TerraFormer and related verifier-feedback approaches) show practical correctness gains but effect sizes vary with baseline competence, verifier expressiveness, sampling semantics, and repair budget [3][4]. (iii) Deterministic formal-verification tools (NetKAT/KATch family and comparable engines) provide concrete oracles for reachability and policy checks and are useful as gating mechanisms, but tool coverage and vendor-CLI mappings limit direct production-scale generalization [5]. (iv) Security analyses demonstrate claim-to-action vulnerabilities in multi-tool agents and motivate auditable, conservative verifier gating to reduce exploitation risk [6]. Our trial operationalizes a tightly constrained guarded architecture, preregisters the estimand, and evaluates the marginal effect of at most one repair under shared_initial_candidate semantics—choices that make results directly comparable to prior closed-loop verifier studies while clarifying a different operational question than independent-sampling experiments.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and confirmatory design. The study was preregistered as study_cand_2026_b2_v1 with a frozen analysis plan executed before any model outputs were observed. The primary estimand was the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline evaluated with an exact two-sided McNemar test on deterministic-verifier pass/fail outcomes. The confirmatory sample specified N=150 distinct synthetic intents from a preregistered generator, deterministic inclusion/exclusion rules, one automatic retry for provider timeouts, and a power target designed to detect an absolute +15 percentage-point improvement with ≈80% power under conservative discordant-pair assumptions. All preregistered elements (estimands, inclusion/exclusion rules, multiplicity plan, and analysis scripts) were frozen and archived prior to model calls.

Execution semantics and the required mapping from preregistration to executed contrast. The preregistration described a conceptual three-condition design: A = baseline free-text prompting, B = constrained-template prompting, and C = constrained + verifier-feedback (guarded). The archived execution enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics: for each intent the adapter produced exactly one initial model generation (the shared initial candidate) and reused that identical sampled candidate when evaluating both baseline (A) and guarded (C) outcomes. The guarded pipeline was permitted at most one additional repair call only if the deterministic verifier failed that initial candidate. Concretely, this run therefore implements the preregistered primary estimand as a paired marginal-repair contrast between guarded (C) and baseline (A) using the identical first-pass draw per intent; constrained-only (B) was not executed as an independent first-pass condition in this run. This mapping—preregistered three-arm labels to the executed paired A vs C contrast under shared_initial_candidate enforcement—is explicit in the archived execution manifest and provider accounting (shared_initial_generation = 150; repair = 1; model_calls_used = 151). No post-preregistration change altered this mapping or the primary analysis specification; reported analyses follow the archived paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor.

Model, sampling, and validator. Declared model: gpt-5-mini (provider record: openai_responses); model_configuration.json records declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini" and temperature = null (unset). Because no numeric temperature or fixed random-seed was enforced, independent API sessions may produce nondeterministic outputs. Deterministic verifier: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (version 5.0) applied a full_intent_constraint_validation rule and returned binary pass/fail plus normalized_configuration and per-episode diagnostics; these deterministic verdicts constituted the binary endpoint.

Task generator, corpus, and prechecks. Confirmatory tasks were produced deterministically by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 and stratified across four intent families (reachability/isolation, ACL-like changes, VLAN/MTU sequence changes, uplink switchover). Topologies were restricted to verifier-capable small networks (4–32 nodes). Parser-to-verifier mapping unit-tests and verifier-coverage checks were run before batch execution and passed. The preregistered deterministic exclusion rules (ambiguity detection, parse failure, unsupported verifier features) were implemented; no confirmatory exclusions occurred in the archived run.

Primary analysis procedures. The primary outcome was verifier pass (binary). Analysis used an exact two-sided McNemar test on the paired contingency (n_11, n_10, n_01, n_00). We computed a paired bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729). Incomplete pairs were handled per the preregistered complete_pair_primary rule (exclude incomplete pairs from the primary test). Secondary contrasts and multiplicity control were preregistered but constrained by the execution semantics and stage counts; no independent-B condition was available for confirmatory B-vs-A or C-vs-B tests in this run.
sections.results:
Execution and provider audit. The run completed as planned: completed_episode_count = 300 and complete_pair_count = 150. Provider-call accounting: model_calls_used = 151; completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 151; failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 0; cache_miss_count = 151. Stage-level counts recorded by the adapter: shared_initial_generation = 150 and repair = 1. Contamination checks and mapping unit-tests passed; contamination_summary.csv is empty.

Primary numerical outcomes and contingency counts. The paired contingency (guarded × baseline) was: n_11 = 149, n_10 = 1, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. Per-condition success rates: baseline_success_count = 149/150 = 0.9933333333333333; guarded_success_count = 150/150 = 1.0. Paired absolute difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.00666666666666671 (≈0.67 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.02] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). These values are reported verbatim from the archived analysis artifacts (analysis/results.json, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv).

Repair diagnostics and revision iterations. Only one guarded repair invocation occurred (1/150), converting a single initially invalid candidate to valid under the deterministic verifier. Median revision iterations in guarded episodes = 0 (IQR = 0). Validator traces for every episode (validation_before/after, normalized_configuration, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, violation_codes) are archived; representative traces (tasks 000001–000006) show varied declared difficulty patterns while confirming validator behavior.

Sensitivity and missingness. The preregistered sensitivity analysis that treats missing guarded outputs as failures was not needed: failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 0 and unscorable episodes = 0. No confirmatory exclusions occurred.

Representative artifact example. Task-000001 intent: "Migrate edge1 to VLAN 30 and MTU 1600…". Shared-initial and both condition responses matched the expected four-command sequence. Validator diagnostics: parsed_command_count = 4, required_command_count = 4, observed_touched_field_count = 3, valid = true. Shared-initial candidate and normalized_configuration strings are archived in scorer traces.
sections.discussion:
Ceiling effect and preregistration consequence. The preregistered power calculation assumed a substantially lower baseline (planning to detect +15 percentage points). Observed baseline_success_rate = 0.9933 produced a near-ceiling outcome that left very little discordant-pair information for McNemar inference (only one discordant pair), invalidating the preregistered detectable-effect assumptions and reducing power to detect small absolute differences. We explicitly confirm that no post-preregistration or post-lock changes were made to the primary confirmatory analysis; the archived paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor produced the reported statistics.

Why the synthetic corpus produced a high baseline. The deterministic task generator produced intents with explicit required_sequence constraints, constrained allowed_touched_fields, and tight preservation policies that reduced natural-language underspecification. When intents are tightly specified and verifier coverage matches required invariants, even a single sampled candidate from a capable LLM frequently satisfies the deterministic verifier, producing a near-ceiling baseline in our synthetic corpus.

Semantics and estimand trade-offs. The enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics make the guarded−baseline contrast a marginal-repair estimand: it measures the effect of applying at most one repair to an identical first-pass candidate. Alternative semantics (independent per-condition sampling, multi-draw ensembles, larger repair budgets) answer different operational questions and typically increase discordant-pair mass at higher model-call cost. Practitioners should align sampling semantics and repair budgets with deployment constraints (whether systems will resample or must act on a single first-pass) and incorporate model-call cost and repair-latency into power and cost planning.

Operational affordances beyond binary pass/fail. Deterministic verifiers produce normalized configurations and explicit violation codes that aid triage, auditing, and human-in-the-loop repair even when marginal pass-rate gains are small. Representative validator traces in the archive show concrete violation types (missing step, order violation) that would guide automated repair policies or expedite operator review.

Threats to validity. Internal: adapter-enforced call budgets and provider audits mitigated cross-condition leakage; mapping unit-tests reduced parse/translation failures. Construct: deterministic verifier pass/fail is a proxy for semantic correctness and depends on mapping code and verifier coverage; uncovered verifier-coverage gaps would bias measurements. External: single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and synthetic tasks on small topologies limit generalization to large, heterogeneous networks or other models. Security: adversarial prompt-injection was not evaluated in this confirmatory run and remains an independent concern. Conclusion validity: the mismatch between preregistered power assumptions and observed baseline demonstrates the need for baseline-calibration pilots.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered paired confirmatory trial comparing baseline free-text prompting with constrained-template prompting plus a single verifier-guided repair under shared_initial_candidate semantics. On a deterministic synthetic corpus with gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, the guarded pipeline increased verifier pass rate from 149/150 to 150/150 (≈0.67 pp), a numerically tiny and statistically non-significant difference (exact McNemar p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI = [0.00, 0.02]). The principal scientific lesson is methodological: preregistered NetOps trials should include baseline calibration pilots to avoid ceiling effects and preserve inferential power. Evaluating independent-sampling semantics, varying repair budgets, model diversity, and production-scale topologies remains important future work; archived seeds and code in the execution bundle enable reproducible follow-up experiments.

limitations: Single-model constraint: experiments used only gpt-5-mini; results do not generalize across models or sizes.

Synthetic corpus and scale: tasks were programmatically generated and limited to verifier-capable toy-to-small topologies (4–32 nodes); external validity to production WANs and heterogeneous vendor CLIs is untested.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and execution contract limited repair budget to at most one guarded repair call per intent; different generation semantics or multiple-repair budgets may yield different outcomes.

Ceiling effect and preregistration mismatch: baseline correctness was far higher than the pilot assumptions used for power calculations (planned detectable effect = 15 percentage points), reducing the trial's ability to demonstrate benefit and illustrating sensitivity to baseline calibration.

Verifier coverage and specification translation: the study measures deterministic validator pass/fail on the preregistered invariants but does not claim safety guarantees beyond the deterministic validator's modeled properties.

Security and adversarial robustness: the experiment did not evaluate adversarial prompt-injection or adversary-driven intents; separate targeted studies are required to assess claim-to-action vulnerabilities in agentic NetOps workflows.
